name: From Bastille to Waterloo
description: How a hungry, indebted France overthrew its king, frightened Europe and gave rise to a general who tried to rule it all.

checkpoints.name: The old regime cracks
checkpoints.note: Enlightenment thinkers question kings and the Church while wars such as the Seven Years' War and the American Revolutionary War drain the French treasury and make reform unavoidable.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and Terror
checkpoints.note: The Bastille falls, the Rights of Man are declared, the king is executed and the republic fights Europe. Under Robespierre fear rules until he too is sent to the guillotine.

checkpoints.name: Bonaparte rises
checkpoints.note: A young general wins fame in Italy and Egypt and seizes power in 1799. In the colonies, enslaved people in Saint-Domingue make their own revolution.

checkpoints.name: Emperor of Europe
checkpoints.note: Napoleon crowns himself emperor, wins at Austerlitz and redraws the map, though Trafalgar leaves Britain master of the seas and Spain bleeds his armies. In 1812 he invades Russia.

checkpoints.name: Fall and exile
checkpoints.note: After Russia, the allies defeat him at Leipzig, he abdicates, returns for a hundred days and is beaten at Waterloo. He is sent to Saint Helena.

checkpoints.name: The aftershocks
checkpoints.note: The settlement made at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 tries to keep the old order in place, but the ideas of 1789 return in 1830 and 1848, when revolutions sweep across the continent.
